title: [review] slot-claim: Rust/C decoders don't enforce ascending payload key order (parity vs Python gate)
description: Security-pass P4 note on cb10 commit 68b709d89a. Python decode_cose now enforces deterministic-CBOR via a canonical re-encode byte-equality gate, which rejects non-ascending payload keys at decode. Rust from_cose (slot.rs:568-603) and C (coap_slot_coord.c) use a seen-bitmask: they reject duplicate/unknown keys but do NOT enforce ascending key order at decode, relying on digest-received-bytes to fail malleated signatures. Net: a key holder who signs a key-reordered payload is accepted by Rust/C but rejected by Python — a three-way verdict asymmetry for non-conformant signers. Fail-safe and contract-conformant (deterministic CBOR is the adjudicated wire form, spec/decisions.jsonl slot-claim-cose-sign1), but if exact three-way verdict parity is desired, Rust/C need the same ascending-key/re-encode enforcement. Related: l2uk tracks Rust's own non-ascending/trailing gap.
